repositories.name: Babel Truth
repositories.notes: Owns transferable foundations, shared operating rules, semantic contracts, registry, and major architecture decisions. ADR 0004 owns the shared Babel shell boundary, ADR 0005 the cross-app context boundary, and ADR 0006 bounded Lab incubation.

repositories.name: Babel FIRE
repositories.notes: Owns FIRE doctrine, production runtime/data, frozen successor shell, specs/tests, and promoted implementation. V6 remains production; G7 is 10/10 Locked and Frozen at runtime anchor 4a258c5170dd1d96dcbc0f2b0a9c35b283cec489. The current FIRE Core Lab specimen is the top-of-product heartbeat; it is evidence pending physical iPhone review, not production behavior.

repositories.name: Babel Lab
repositories.notes: Lab is evidence, never authority. It hosts Shell Gallery plus isolated Fire Lab and World Lab experiments using fake/local state by default. FIRE Core may audition bounded unproven interaction behavior here without moving product ownership. WORLD Phase 1 remains a Lab product audition and does not yet justify a standalone WORLD repository.

repositories.name: Babel World
repositories.role: future optional artist-development and creative-context product
repositories.notes: WORLD Phase 1 lives under babel-lab/world/context-loop/. A real WORLD product earns its own repo only after physical use proves independent orientation/decision value beyond a single exact scenario.

repositories.name: Babel ARC
repositories.role: time and capacity coordination product candidate
repositories.notes: ARC means Adapt → Reconcile → Coordinate. Its distinct job is to reconcile commitments, responsibilities, capacity, and changing reality into an executable schedule. It has not earned a standalone repo, backend, runtime, or visual UI; first prove the headless conversation → reconcile → calendar loop in real use. Future cross-app scheduling handoffs should carry only the smallest useful intent under ADR 0005.
